title: Ramp cascade failure scratchpad
content:
Quick scratchpad from yesterday's weird cascade during a synthetic ramp test. Goal: reproduce a repeatable p99 spike during a gentle ramp (5->200 qps over 120s) that then triggers queue growth and eventually evicts warm KV entries leading to a larger cold-cache penalty. Hypothesis: combination of batch timeout + KV cache eviction under memory pressure + preemption/replacement in the GPU hotpool.

Setup:
- Model: redwood/open-7b-qlora (quantized checkout from /models/q7b-v2)
- Fleet: 4x A10G dedicated nodes, 4 workers each, 16GB per worker (hotpool enabled)
- Runtime: serving-runtime@main (PR 498 candidate patch applied: adaptive-batch-timeout=8ms)
- Traffic: synthetic generator (zipfian ingress with 5s microbursts every 30s), ramp profile linear 5->200 qps over 120s, TTL for KV entries 180s
- Observed metric window: 2024-10-28 14:02 - 14:18 (UTC)

Observations / raw notes:
- Initial ramp (5->50 qps) stable: p50 ~ 20ms, p95 ~ 45ms, p99 ~ 88ms
- Around 80 qps p95 starts to oscillate +/-30ms; p99 had small spikes to 180ms coinciding with microbursts
- At ~140 qps a sustained p99 plateau appears (~420ms) for ~60s; request queue length increased from ~3->28
- During plateau, KV cache hit-rate dropped 92% -> 58% over ~90s (seen in console trace)
- Heap pressure + GPU hotpool evictions logged (eviction events correlate with KV miss spike)
- When hotpool evictions happened we saw synchronous reloading: tail latency jumped to 1.2s for a small subset (3-5%) of requests

Quick ascii timeline (approx):
T: qps 5->200 (120s)
[00-30s] qps 5-50: stable p99 < 100ms
[30-70s] qps 50-120: oscillations, microburst spikes up to 200ms
[70-90s] qps 120-160: queue climbs, KV miss spike begins
[90-140s] qps 160-200: sustained p99 plateau 400-1200ms, eviction logs flood

Immediate hypotheses:
- Adaptive-batch-timeout at 8ms is too aggressive for this traffic shape; cross-request batching increases variability and holds more in-flight state leading to memory pressure and more KV churn.
- Hotpool eviction policy favors fairness but doesn't account for sequential locality; working set churn causes repeated reloads.
- Microbursts create transient queue depth that interacts badly with the current autoscaler settings (scale-up lag + sticky warmup).

Next steps / experiments:
1) Re-run with adaptive-batch-timeout=4ms and 16ms to measure sensitivity (keep everything else constant).
2) Increase KV TTL from 180s -> 600s for a run to see if hit-rate stabilizes (but be mindful of memory footprint).
3) Toggle hotpool eviction policy off (or use LRU->LFU) for an A/B run to see change in tail behavior.
4) Add a short prefix caching prefetch for streaming sessions (cheap experiment in client shim).
5) Correlate with autoscaler metrics: pod spin-up delay and GPU allocation logs for the plateau window.

Notes for PR/issue: file a concise bug for PLAT-1423 with attached flamegraph snippets and the small CSV export (p50/p95/p99/queue_len/kv_hit) I dumped to /tmp (will upload). Mention candidate mitigation in PR 498 but we may need combined fixes (batching + cache policy + autoscale tuning).

Open questions / things I forgot to capture:
- Did we see vGPU preemption events? need kernel logs from nodes 02-03.
- Are any multi-tenant noisy neighbors present? the test cluster had a stray job on node-03 during the window.
- Confirm the generator's client-side timeout: some clients were retried and may have inflated queue.

Quick conclusion (scratch): not purely a batching bug — it's a multi-factor cascade (batching timing x cache churn x scale lag). Experiment matrix above should reveal dominant factor. Prioritize smaller parameter sweeps (timeout + TTL) before bigger infra changes.

Patch notes to self: capture per-request trace ids for next run (add header X-TRACE-ID), increase trace sampling to 20% for 10m around the planned run.

-- fiona
